review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Bakeware, specialised kitchen tools and food-preparation actions; opener intersections, instrument/patient direction and malformed inherited action terms.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. King Arthur Baking, OXO and a culinary-training curriculum support selected tool and action distinctions. Source definitions are not copied; scope restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 and unspecified strength. Shape, removable-wall construction and purpose are separate axes. A combined opener has two supported genera. Preserve earlier kitchen families and their direct genus checks.

sense_decisions.scope: A baking vessel that gives food its form; exclude non-food moulds.
An oblong baking mould for loaf-shaped food, including bread and cakes.
A baking mould with individual muffin wells, without a fixed well count.
A baking mould with a removable locking sidewall.
A baking mould restricted by round shape.
The intersection of round shape and removable locking sidewall.
The oven-roasting vessel, excluding the cook and food senses of roaster.
A baking tray intended for cookies. Retain the existing broader tray rather than importing the whole synonym cluster.
A utensil for crushing garlic; correct the dictionary restriction to extracting juice.
A kitchen tool for removing an apple core. Do not equate coring with peeling.
The hand-operated food-can opening device. The existing glass jar is not its generic patient.
A bottle-opening tool for crown caps. The general bottle-opening family also includes corkscrews.
A combined tool with both cork-extraction and crown-cap-opening functions.
A knife intended for food preparation.
A small kitchen knife used for peeling and trimming food. Keep it distinct from the separate vegetable-peeler device.
A kitchen knife intended to slice bread; a blade material is not specified.
A general-purpose kitchen knife for food cutting.
A tool for cutting cookie shapes from dough; exclude the figurative standardized-person meaning.
A rolling-blade utensil for cutting pizza, narrower than all pizza-cutting tools.
A food-preparation brush for applying a surface coating.
A bag used to pipe a culinary mixture.
The pastry-work scraper used on a work surface, excluding bowl scrapers, building tools and paint spatulas.
The food-preparation action that removes an apple core; distinguish the action from its tool.
Applying a coating to food; a restricted food-preparation sense of the broader smearing action.
Extruding a culinary mixture through a pastry-bag opening for shaping or decoration. Exclude fluid transport through plumbing.
The cutting of cookie shapes from dough before baking, distinct from cutting a baked cookie.
Reuse the broader baking tray; do not import a second general tray from the cookie-sheet synset.
The existing brush has drawing/painting context. A broader brush family requires separate review before reparenting the pastry brush.
The existing spatula is not automatically identical to a bench scraper or food-turning utensil.
The existing jar has glass-material context and is not reused as a generic metal food can.
Preserve the reviewed vegetable-peeler device and its purpose; the paring knife receives no peeler genus.
Inherited steel and iron assertions and knife/tool exclusions remain queued for material and functional-tool review.
The inherited scissors dependency and other old quantified targets remain queued; only the reversed knife-patient assertion is rejected.
The remaining peeling/slicing coordinate assertion is retained pending a distinct review of action overlap.
The spelling чеснокодавилка is attested in the normative orthographic dictionary: https://gramota.ru/storage/public/normdicts/orfograficheskij_slovar.pdf

review.limits: No brands, prices, preferred materials, dimensions, well counts, recipes or operating instructions are imported. Existing painting-brush, generic spatula and glass-jar senses are not reused as broader kitchen-brush, pastry-scraper or food-can concepts. Knife materials, generic cutting dependencies, inherited food-patient specificity and the peeling/slicing coordinate relation require separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject the opener/corkscrew exclusion before adding the supported subtype and intersection. Add no exclusions and preserve all explicit negations.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing bakeware, baking tray, knife, bottle opener, corkscrew and food actions are reused. New pan and tool restrictions do not import entire polysemous dictionary clusters.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.

repairs.reason: A corkscrew is a kind of bottle-opening tool. Retain the broader tool ancestor. OEWN 2025: oewn-03113801-n.

The broad bottle opener and corkscrew cannot be mutually exclusive. Combined corkscrew and cap-opening tools also demonstrate overlap among the narrower functions. Source: https://www.oxo.com/blog/coffee-and-beverages/which-wine-opener-is-right-for-you
Peeling is not a universal prerequisite to slicing food; bread can be sliced without a peeling step. Leave process sequencing to a specified preparation context. OEWN 2025: oewn-02897203-n.
The generic cutting action does not have a knife as its patient merely because a knife can perform cutting. Existing knife purpose and capability assertions already encode the tool role.
